title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཉེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 177)
shelf_note: A Pramāṇa-section commentary (on the Pramāṇavārttika, Pramāṇasiddhi material on rebirth, craving and wrong cognition) in a Derge woodblock print; belongs on the Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa shelf.

ocr_errors.problem: vowel e dropped from གེགས 'obstruction'; recoverable

ocr_errors.image: གཟུགས་ལ་སོགས་པའི་འབྲས་བུའི་རྟེན་ཡིན་ནོ (as far as I can read)
ocr_errors.problem: genitive འི on འབྲས་བུ apparently dropped

tr_errors_A.english: The self-nature of the self as an enjoyer is contradictory because it is characterized by being devoid of action and enjoyment
tr_errors_A.problem: Source says what is contradictory TO the enjoyer-self's nature is the state of being devoid of action and enjoyment; A makes the self-nature itself contradictory 'because' it is devoid of them, garbling the svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhi argument
Sanskrit 'original' asserted in a note; not on the page (plausible reconstruction presented as fact)

tr_errors_A.english: how scripture is not a valid means of knowledge <note>in certain contexts</note>
tr_errors_A.problem: invented hedging qualifier not in the source

tr_errors_A.english: arise together in their respective ways
tr_errors_A.problem: drops 'with that' (the mind/sense base they co-arise with)

tr_errors_A.english: That which is produced immediately after is the basis.
tr_errors_A.problem: adds 'is the basis' from the next lemma; the source only says the capacity is that which arises immediately after

tr_errors_A.english: the attainment of another state, such as the fruit of form and so forth, is the basis
tr_errors_A.problem: misconstrued: attaining another state is the basis OF fruits such as form; A makes form an instance of the attainment

tr_errors_B.problem: སྐྱེ་བ 'arises' rendered as active 'produces'; slight shift
'beings' for embodied things (flames are the example); small slip

pages.prefer_reason: B construes the opening svabhāvaviruddhopalabdhi argument and the closing 'basis of fruits such as form' correctly, where A garbles both and adds unsupported notes.

book_verdict: Clean Derge print with a near-accurate transcription; both translations are serviceable, but B is the more faithful and A has several moderate construal errors and two invented notes.
